spec.title: Mars base on Jezero
assumptions: Terrain: real elevation data, Jezero Crater, Mars (40 m square, 15.5 m of relief, typical slope 18.2°). Credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona HiRISE; DTM via USGS on AWS Open Data (CC0 1.0).
Selected a larger measured Jezero Crater, Mars patch: 39.646 m to 80.308 m for full structure footprints and 1 m setbacks; source elevations were not stretched or flattened.
Gave the robot up to 62 s to reach the goal: 20.7 m at about 0.83 m/s, times 2.5, kept within 20–120 s.
You named Mars, so the world is Mars.
Added trench, not in the terrain data.

structural_check.honesty: 2D aluminium portal rib, 10 frame elements, fixed bases; the visual model isn't analysed
structural_check.assumptions: 6061-T6 nominal SHS, E=69 GPa, assumed yield 240 MPa; yield / 1.5; axial plus bending stress; displacement limit diameter/360. One portal rib approximates an arch; equipment and projected-roof shielding shared by tributary length. Nodal gravity loads; no pressure shell, skin mass, joints, buckling, lateral stability or foundation analysis. Screening, not certification.

structural_check.summary: 2% under landing what-if: 3 x local gravity (static equivalent) (stress, member 1).
structural_check.honesty: 2D aluminium frame, 2 opposite legs + body, pinned feet; the visual model isn't analysed
structural_check.assumptions: Assumed body mass 2000 kg. 6061-T6 nominal SHS, E=69 GPa, assumed yield 240 MPa; yield / 1.5; combined axial/bending leg stress; Euler K=1 with leg-length restraint in both planes. One opposite pair carries half the assumed body mass plus its own frame weight. No body strength, propellant, impact dynamics, joints, terrain compliance or lateral-system analysis. Screening, not certification.

structure_notes: Habitat on 5.0° ground, 48 m from the goal.
Lander on 3.8° ground, 21 m from the start.
Bridge spans a 1.82 m path gap (span 2.83 m, 0.5 m bearings).
